paper_type_rationale: The paper proposes a trained vision-language reasoning model, Qwen-LookAgain, using cold start data, rule-based reinforcement learning, supervised fine-tuning, and visual token re-attention mechanisms.
dominant_domain: Vision-language reasoning, hallucination reduction, visual token dilution, reinforcement learning, reflective multimodal reasoning.
must_cover: Long VLRM reasoning dilutes visual tokens and can increase hallucination.
Text-only reflection does not sufficiently restore attention to visual tokens.
BRPO trains the model to decide when to generate reflection and to balance reflection count and length.
Qwen-Zero generates Qwen-Zero-40k, which is manually and model-verified for supervised fine-tuning.
Visual Token COPY inserts all original visual tokens before reflection, while Visual Token ROUTE inserts top-attended visual tokens.
Qwen-LA improves visual QA accuracy and hallucination metrics while adding inference overhead.
key_numbers: Qwen-LA-COPY on Table 1: MMMU 60.3, MMMU-Pro 41.7, MMBench 82.7, MMStar 65.9, MathVision 26.4.
Qwen-LA-ROUTE on Table 1: MMMU 59.1, MMMU-Pro 41.3, MMBench 82.8, MMStar 64.6, MathVision 25.8.
Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct baseline: MMMU 58.6, MMMU-Pro 41.0, MMBench 82.6, MMStar 63.9, MathVision 25.1.
Table 2 hallucination: Qwen-LA-COPY CHAIRi 3.7, CHAIRs 9.8, POPE 90.2, MMHAL 3.82, MME 2330.8.
Table 3 overhead on MMMU: Qwen2.5-VL 58.6 accuracy and 8.68s; Qwen-LA-COPY 60.3 and 22.33s; Qwen-LA-ROUTE 59.1 and 18.29s.
Ablation Table 4: text-only BRPO without VTC/VTR reaches 58.8 MMMU and CHAIRi 8.7, while Qwen-LA-COPY reaches 60.3 and CHAIRi 3.7.
Visual Token ROUTE uses m=50 by default; Table 5 shows larger m improves accuracy and hallucination but increases latency.
BRPO training uses 8 NVIDIA A800-SXM4 80G GPUs for 48 hours; cold start uses 2k examples and Qwen-Zero distills 40k examples.
real_comparisons: Compared with text-only reflection, Qwen-LA adds visual tokens at reflection positions to force visual re-attention.
Compared with PAI, which adjusts attention weights, Qwen-LA physically supplements visual tokens through copy or route.
Compared with ICoT, which adds local image-feature prompts before reasoning paragraphs, Qwen-LA targets reflection moments.
Compared with non-reasoning Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen-LA improves accuracy and hallucination metrics at higher inference cost.

central_claims.claim: Long vision-language reasoning reduces attention to visual tokens and can increase hallucination.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: The paper provides MSCOCO analyses and a formal ratio-based argument that visual-token proportion declines as generation grows.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: The proof assumes visual neglect is an important cause of hallucination and does not cover every hallucination mechanism.

central_claims.claim: Vision-text reflection with visual re-attention is more effective than text-only or vision-only reflection.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: Table 6 and Table 4 show Qwen-LA-COPY and Qwen-LA-ROUTE outperform text-only and vision-only reflection settings on key metrics.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove that copy or route is the optimal way to select visual evidence.

central_claims.claim: BRPO helps the model learn when and how much to reflect.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: Figure 6 and Figure 7 show more frequent but shorter reflections and rising test accuracy during training; Table 4 shows performance drops without BRPO.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not isolate BRPO from all effects of cold-start data quality and the Qwen-Zero-40k distillation process.

claim_boundaries: The implementation is based on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct due to resource limits.
Visual re-attention improves performance but increases inference overhead.
The theoretical analysis assumes hallucination is partly caused by visual information neglect.
Some training data is generated by GPT-4o and Qwen-Zero, then verified, so data quality is a key dependency.
negative_or_limiting_results: Text-only reflection does not reduce hallucination in the initial analysis.
Without BRPO, models with visual re-attention have unstable or weaker performance.
Using BRPO without visual token copy or route is not optimal; CHAIRi remains 8.7.
Small ROUTE ratio m=25 reduces model accuracy, while larger m increases latency.
VTC and VTR overhead may be unacceptable in instant-response settings.
mechanism_result_map: BRPO format, accuracy, and reflection-balance rewards map to Qwen-Zero's multi-stage reflection behavior.
Qwen-Zero-40k distillation maps to supervised training of Qwen-LA-COPY and Qwen-LA-ROUTE.
Visual Token COPY maps to higher accuracy and stronger hallucination reduction, but higher sequence length and latency.
Visual Token ROUTE maps to lower overhead than COPY, with slightly weaker but still competitive metrics.
Increasing m in VTR maps to higher accuracy and hallucination scores but increased runtime.
comparative_positioning: Qwen-LA is a training-based counterpart to TrainingFree visual revisiting methods such as VisRef and SDR-MCoT.
Unlike PRCR, Qwen-LA does not optimize cache reuse; it learns behavior and modifies visual-token flow during reflection.
Compared with Position: Your VLM May Not Be Thinking with Interleaved Images, Qwen-LA must be read with the question of whether re-attended visual tokens are truly causal.
Compared with Qwen Look Again's base model, the gains are modest in accuracy but larger in hallucination reduction.
reuse_takeaways: Reflection should be tied to actual visual evidence refresh, not only text prompts.
For 3D agents, use reflection moments as hooks to reinsert rendered views, point subsets, or spatial memory.
Report inference overhead together with hallucination reduction.
Ablate behavior learning, text reflection, and visual evidence insertion separately.
followup_questions: Would VTR work better with diversity-aware visual token selection rather than top-attention selection?
Can PRCR-style cache reuse reduce the overhead of VTC/VTR?
How much of Qwen-LA's gain comes from Qwen-Zero-40k data quality versus visual token reinsertion?
Does Qwen-LA still use the copied or routed tokens under causal removal tests?
